note: Largest solar flare of Solar Cycle 25 to date. Erupted from Active Region 3664 on the solar limb. Associated with rapid proton flux enhancement and coronal mass ejection.
source: NASA DONKI / NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
operationalGuidance: Radiation shelter protocol recommended for interplanetary crews. For LEO / ISS, monitor South Atlantic Anomaly passes and high-latitude orbital geomagnetically induced proton flux.

note: Major Earth-directed X-class flare occurring during the peak of the G5 Extreme Geomagnetic Storm. Extensive radio blackout (R3) across the Pacific region.
source: NASA DONKI / NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
operationalGuidance: G5 Extreme storm conditions. High-voltage power grid and satellite communication precautions active. Astronauts in LEO advised to sleep in shielded central modules (Node 2 / Zvezda).

note: Powerful flare producing fast halo coronal mass ejection (>1200 km/s) that merged with preceding CMEs into a 'cannibal' CME structure triggering global G5 geomagnetic conditions.
operationalGuidance: Fast CME transit time (~28 hours to Earth). Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) suspended; verify crew dosimeter badge readings before and after SAA passes.

note: Early eruptive flare from the precursor phase of the May 2024 storm sequence. Marked the onset of elevated energetic electron and proton fluxes at GEO and LEO altitudes.
operationalGuidance: Initial advisory issued to flight control team. Telemetry checks on external robotic arms and solar array drive mechanisms.

note: Opening X-class flare initiating the active storm period. High-frequency communication degradation observed on dayside Earth.
operationalGuidance: Standard space-weather monitoring advisory. Maintain normal flight operations while tracking Active Region 3664 rotation toward central meridian.
